title: Why earthquake sizes use a logarithmic scale
examples: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?
How much bigger is a magnitude 7 than a magnitude 6?
What does a logarithmic scale do?

items.label: Magnitude 7
items.ask: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?

explain.say: When an earthquake hits, a machine called a seismograph draws a wobbly line. The bigger the quake, the taller the wobbles. Look at the first bar: a magnitude 4 quake. Let us call its wobble size 1.

draw.text: Why earthquake sizes use a logarithmic scale

items.label: Magnitude 7
items.ask: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?

explain.say: Now a magnitude 5. Its wobbles are 10 times taller. See the second bar? Just one step up the scale, but ten times the shaking. Does that surprise you?

items.label: Magnitude 7
items.ask: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?

explain.say: Magnitude 6 is 10 times bigger again: 100 times the magnitude 4. Look at the third bar. And the magnitude 4 bar is already hard to see!

items.label: Magnitude 7
items.ask: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?

explain.say: Magnitude 7, the last bar, is 1000 times the shaking of a magnitude 4. If we drew these on a normal scale, the small ones would vanish. A log scale counts the times ten instead, so 4, 5, 6, 7 stay easy to read.

items.label: Magnitude 7
items.ask: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?

explain.say: Well done! Each step also releases about 32 times more energy. The 2011 quake in Japan was magnitude 9.1: a thousand times the energy of a magnitude 7. Sound in decibels and acidity in pH use the same trick.

faq.q: Why is the Richter scale logarithmic?
faq.a: Earthquakes range from tiny tremors to giant shocks millions of times bigger. A log scale counts powers of ten, so the whole range fits on a scale from about 1 to 10.
asks: Why do we use a log scale for earthquakes?

faq.a: Magnitude is a number for the size of an earthquake, worked out from how big the seismograph wobbles are. Each whole step means ten times bigger wobbles.

faq.q: How much bigger is a magnitude 7 than a magnitude 6?
faq.a: The ground shaking is 10 times bigger, and the energy released is about 32 times bigger.
asks: How many times stronger is each magnitude?

faq.a: A seismograph is an instrument that records ground shaking as a wavy line. Taller waves mean stronger shaking.
Decibels for loudness, pH for acidity, and star brightness are all logarithmic. Each step means multiplying, not adding.
asks: Where else are log scales used?

facts: Each whole step on the Richter magnitude scale means ten times larger seismograph wave amplitude and about 32 times more energy.
The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake in Japan had a magnitude of about 9.0 to 9.1.
